title: Atlantic City's clubs, Million Dollar Pier and boardwalk
summary: Atlantic City had the Million Dollar Pier, the Silver Slipper, Paradise and many clubs, whose bills were much richer than today's one-star shows.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: or Atlantic City had. Atlantic City had the Million Dollar Pier where all the big bands played.
And they had, like, all the Clubs like the Silver Slipper. Then you had the big colored clubs like the Paradise and other clubs.
The gambling, you didn't have a lot of gambling back there. If it was gambling, it was private. They never did have too much gambling.
But the Boardwalk was a big thing in Atlantic City that drew people there -- the water and the boardwalk was fabulous, you know. Salt water taffee (inaudible).
The nightclub business in Atlantic City was good. Had a lot of clubs in Atlantic City, much more than they have now.
They got -- you got your places like Caesar's Palace, and things like that.

But even as I look at those places today, that the money that you're paying to go and see what they have there, like the Sammy Davis (inaudible), what're you going to see? You're going to see one artist.
You go -- (inaudible) Anybody go there. Tony

An hour and a half -- an hour a show. I mean, every act that went out on the floor just knocked you over. When you leave there, you'd say, "Oh man, we gotta go back to Small's Paradise." You know, got to go to the Silver Slipper.

You go to -- Steel Craig got two big bands. Fletcher Henderson, another big white band -- to any of them, you know. Coon- (Inaudible) Sanders, or whoever would come in there, you know -- and all these other things happening there.
Atlantic City was really a playground, really. The, of course, when the Depression hit it,

But even then, everybody was going to Atlantic City, because it was the cheapest place that you can go and enjoy yourself.

You can stay on the beach, if you had money, you know, you can go to the hotels where they had bands -- things like that.

Then all out from Atlantic City, up and down the streets there, you had other whatever clubs. You had the White Elephant, (inaudible) -- club in (inaudible) the White Elephant, way down at the end of the boardwalk.

And Atlantic City was a place -- what it was supposed to be, like what they're trying to make it now.

Atlantic City is not Atlantic City -- turn into a gambling place. If you go on the boardwalk, you'll find more people in the casinos now. You see nobody on the don't (inaudible) boardwalk too much.

There are people that ride up and down the boardwalk. You (inaudible) used to walk from one end of the boardwalk -- the boardwalk was a showplace.
